site.title: Janani Pradhaban | Bharatanatyam Dancer, Teacher and Organ Donation Advocate
site.description: Janani Pradhaban is a classical Bharatanatyam dancer and teacher, a liver transplant recipient and a volunteer for organ donation awareness.

person.name: Janani Pradhaban
person.tagline: Carrying India's timeless art to the world stage
person.heroQuote: A gift of life can become a lifetime of hope.

about.heading: Meet Janani
about.intro: Janani Pradhaban is a classical Bharatanatyam dancer and teacher, a wife, a mother and a liver transplant recipient. Her life has been a journey through dreams, unexpected challenges, renewed hope and profound gratitude.
about.imageAlt: Janani Pradhaban standing in a dark block-printed saree
about.family: She was born into a family associated with India's Defence Production establishment. Her father, Mr. G. Pradhaban, is a retired Indian Ordnance Factories Service (IOFS) officer, and her mother is Mrs. Malini Pradhaban. Their love and encouragement became the foundation of her life.

stats.label: dance forms studied: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Western
performances a week at her peak

paragraphs: From the age of four, Janani began learning Bharatanatyam. What started as a childhood interest soon became her greatest passion, an essential part of her identity and a source of happiness.

Alongside Bharatanatyam she explored Western dance, Kathak and Odissi. She completed her Salangai Pujai and her Arangetram, and performed at temple festivals, cultural celebrations and prestigious stages.
At one stage she was performing almost twice a week, and she dreamed of releasing her own dance album.
about.quote: I felt a star living her dream.

art.heading: Born in India's Temples
art.imageAlt: Golden statue of Nataraja, Shiva as the cosmic dancer, within a ring of flames, standing on a lotus base
art.imageCaption: Nataraja, Shiva as Lord of Dance: the divine inspiration behind the art
points: Born in the temples of Tamil Nadu and danced as an offering to the divine
Drawn from the Natyashastra, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts
One of India's eight classical dance forms, recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi

margam.heading: A Recital in Seven Movements
margam.intro: The traditional order of a solo Bharatanatyam performance, the margam, from invocation to benediction.

items.name: Tillana
items.text: A joyous, fast finale of rhythm and pattern

items.name: Mangalam
items.text: A closing prayer of thanks and blessing

margam.note: Some recitals vary the order or add items.

guru.heading: Learning at the Guru's Side
guru.imageAlt: Janani's guru gently guiding her arm position in a Bharatanatyam pose against a black backdrop
guru.label: Guru Smt. Malathi Vaidyanatham
guru.text: Bharatanatyam is traditionally passed from teacher to student, one gesture at a time. Janani learned the art at her guru's side, and today she passes it on to students of her own.

prayer.heading: Prayer Before Performance

images.alt: A Bharatanatyam dancer in an orange and gold costume kneeling with folded hands before a temple altar with oil lamps and flower garlands
Wide view of the dancer at prayer before the temple altar

points: Dancers traditionally begin with a prayer, seeking blessings before every performance
Salangai Pujai: the ceremony that blesses a dancer's ankle bells
The art itself began as an offering in the temples of Tamil Nadu

backstage.heading: Preparing for the Stage
backstage.imageAlt: A woman applying finishing touches of makeup to a Bharatanatyam dancer in a red costume before a performance
points: Hours of preparation: make-up, jewellery, flowers and costume
Bold eye make-up carries every expression to the last row of the hall
Every adornment has meaning and purpose

diagnosis.heading: Diagnosis and the Long Wait

stats.label: age when her health began to fail
years waiting for a donor liver

cards.title: The diagnosis
cards.text: From the age of 13 her health began to fail and dance had to stop. She was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis, though she had never had jaundice and danced every day.

cards.title: Daily life
cards.text: Before the transplant she had lost almost all her hair, her nails had turned black, her skin had darkened, and even daily routines were extremely difficult.

cards.title: The long wait
cards.text: For five years her family prayed, visited places of worship and held on to hope while waiting for a suitable donor liver. The doctors had explained the risks of surgery, but without a transplant her life was in serious danger.

diagnosis.pullQuote: I was frightened, but I continued to hope.

steps.title: The call
steps.text: A donor family agrees to donate. Reach the hospital within an hour.

steps.title: Admission
steps.text: A night of tests and analysis, with family beside her.

steps.title: The theatre
steps.text: She prays: "Give me a new life. My family is waiting outside."

steps.title: The surgery
steps.text: 20+ people give blood and plasma. The surgery is a success.

steps.title: Into ICU
steps.text: Glass walls, wires, machines and nurses beside her.

steps.title: Intensive care
steps.text: Her family visits and the pain fades, then she moves to the ward.

steps.title: Back home
steps.text: No visitors, to avoid infection. Hair, nails and skin recover.

resilience.heading: Art Shaped by Resilience
resilience.imageAlt: Janani in a hospital bed cutting a small cake, with a baby's bassinet beside her

steps.title: Recovery
steps.text: Five days of close care, then the ward and a long road of medicines, tests and counselling.

steps.title: Renewal
steps.text: Back home, a new life began: her hair, nails and skin recovered, and strength returned.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: She danced again, welcomed a healthy baby on 28 September 2017, and now performs and teaches with deeper purpose.

blessing.heading: A Gift for Her Son
blessing.imageAlt: A doctor in scrubs gently holding a newborn baby wrapped in a blue blanket
blessing.caption: Dr. Mohamed Rela, carrying Janani's son
blessing.label: A Doctor's Blessing
blessing.text: Dr. Mohamed Rela is carrying Janani's son. He gifted a gold chain to her son.
blessing.quote: A miracle in the very next year: February 2016 was her transplantation, and in 2017 her son was born.
blessing.doNotSay: Do NOT state or imply that Dr. Rela was Janani's treating doctor or surgeon. He only carried her son and gifted the gold chain.

gratitude.heading: To the Donor and the Donor's Family
paragraphs: There is one family to whom Janani will always owe a debt of gratitude. In a time of profound grief they chose to donate the organs of a loved one, and because of their generosity she could return to her family, dance again and become a mother.

She may never know their names or meet them, but their decision remains a permanent part of her life story. She also honours the people who donated blood and plasma during her surgery, and the doctors, nurses and healthcare professionals who helped her recover.
gratitude.quote: I honour their decision by living with gratitude and purpose.

seekingBlessings.imageAlt: A dancer in an orange costume bows to touch the feet of a woman holding a tray of offerings, a gesture of respect and blessing, with onlookers in the background
seekingBlessings.caption: A gesture of respect and blessing

mission.heading: Art with Purpose
mission.organisation: Mohan Foundation (Multi Organ Harvesting Aid Network), India
mission.intro: Janani uses her platform to raise awareness of organ donation, volunteering with Mohan Foundation (Multi Organ Harvesting Aid Network) in India.
mission.headlineQuote: One donor can save multiple lives.
mission.personalQuote: Organ donation is not just a cause for me. It is my life story.

reasons.title: Honour my donor
reasons.text: Live with purpose, and say thank you to a donor and family I may never meet.

reasons.title: Share my story
reasons.text: If it inspires even one person to support organ donation, a life may be saved.

reasons.title: Start family conversations
reasons.text: Encourage people to talk with their families about their wishes.

reasons.title: Spread awareness
reasons.text: Help people learn what organ donation is, and register if it is right for them.

callToAction.heading: One yes can save many lives
steps: Talk to your family about your wishes
Register as a donor, if it feels right to you

messageToTheWorld: My life has taught me that hope can survive even in the most difficult circumstances.
My journey is a story of survival, but it is also a story of human kindness.
May my story encourage more people to learn, talk, and consider how they can help others.
mission.disclaimer: Organ donation is a deeply personal decision. For accurate information, please speak to qualified healthcare professionals and authorised organisations such as Mohan Foundation.
